title: 1901, July 4 Somerville view of the official opening of the bridge
description: On July 4, 1901, Premier Tweedie and his colleagues arrived by train in the mid-afternoon and were greeted by an impressive procession. Leading the way was S. S. Miller, Parade Marshall, on horseback, followed by a brass band, decorated bicycles, and a carriage carrying the Directors of the Hartland Bridge Company. Other buckboard wagons transported Members of Parliament and representatives from the Foresters and the Women’s Christian Temperance Union. A large crowd of citizens joined the parade as it moved from the train station through the festively decorated town, across the new bridge to Victoria Corner, and back to a platform on the bridge’s east side, where the official opening ceremony was held. (Archives P61-442)
